title: Token Usage to Energy, Carbon, and Cost
description: This example converts measured token counts and generation time into energy use, two carbon estimates, and a hosted-model cost comparison.

steps.description: We start with one evaluation run: 40 calls, 48,200 input tokens, 6,900 output tokens, and 410 seconds of generation time.
Every assumption is labeled with its source or marked as an assumption to replace: machine wattage, grid carbon intensity, per-token carbon rates, training emissions share, and hosted model prices.
The conversions compute energy in kWh, carbon from measured time, carbon from per-token rates (plus training share), and the hosted price we avoided by running locally.

steps.question: Which carbon estimate is larger: the one from measured time or the one from per-token rates?
steps.answer: Carbon from measured time (1.196 g) is much larger than carbon from per-token rates (0.037 g).

steps.description: The first print shows energy: 3.42 Wh.
Carbon from measured time: 1.196 g CO2e.
Carbon from per-token rates: 0.037 g CO2e, plus 0.156 g training share.
Hosted price avoided: $1.14, plus 0.0034 kWh at your electricity rate.
